1→"""The identity directory — who a principal is, which groups they are in, their native account ids.
   2→
   3→It is a CACHE of the company's identity source (for the demo: ``world.json``'s ``directory``;
   4→native platforms stay authoritative and Gate 2 asks them). Nested groups are expanded once at load.
   5→Every change bumps ``epoch`` so Gate-1 readable-set caches never survive a directory change.
   6→"""
   7→from __future__ import annotations
   8→
   9→import json
  10→import threading
  11→from pathlib import Path
  12→from typing import Iterable, Optional
  13→
  14→from .models import DirectoryUser, UserKind
  15→
  16→
  17→def _expand_groups(groups: list[dict]) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
  18→    """group id → every user id in it, member_groups expanded transitively (cycle-safe)."""
  19→    direct = {g["id"]: set(g.get("members", [])) for g in groups}
  20→    children = {g["id"]: list(g.get("member_groups", [])) for g in groups}
  21→    out: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
  22→
  23→    def walk(gid: str, seen: frozenset) -> set[str]:
  24→        if gid in out:
  25→            return out[gid]
  26→        if gid in seen:
  27→            return set()
  28→        users = set(direct.get(gid, set()))
  29→        for child in children.get(gid, []):
  30→            users |= walk(child, seen | {gid})
  31→        return users
  32→
  33→    for gid in direct:
  34→        out[gid] = walk(gid, frozenset())
  35→    return out
  36→
  37→
  38→class Directory:
  39→    def __init__(self, users: Iterable[DirectoryUser]) -> None:
  40→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
  41→        self._users: dict[str, DirectoryUser] = {u.id: u for u in users}
  42→        self._by_native: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}
  43→        self.epoch = 1
  44→        self._reindex()
  45→
  46→    # -- construction ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  47→    @classmethod
  48→    def from_world(cls, world: dict) -> "Directory":
  49→        d = world.get("directory", {})
  50→        members_of = _expand_groups(d.get("groups", []))
  51→        user_groups: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
  52→        for gid, uids in members_of.items():
  53→            for uid in uids:
  54→                user_groups.setdefault(uid, set()).add(gid)
  55→        users = []
  56→        for u in d.get("users", []):
  57→            groups = set(u.get("groups", [])) | user_groups.get(u["id"], set())
  58→            # a user listed in a child group is also in every ancestor group
  59→            for gid, uids in members_of.items():
  60→                if u["id"] in uids:
  61→                    groups.add(gid)
  62→            users.append(DirectoryUser(
  63→                id=u["id"], name=u.get("name", u["id"]), email=u["email"],
  64→                employment=u.get("employment", "employee"),
  65→                kind=UserKind(u.get("kind", "member")), active=bool(u.get("active", True)),
  66→                roles=tuple(u.get("roles", ["employee"])), groups=tuple(sorted(groups)),
  67→                platform_ids=dict(u.get("platform_ids", {}))))
  68→        return cls(users)
  69→
  70→    @classmethod
  71→    def from_world_file(cls, path: Path) -> "Directory":
  72→        return cls.from_world(json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
  73→
  74→    def _reindex(self) -> None:
  75→        self._by_native = {(p, nid): u.id for u in self._users.values()
  76→                           for p, nid in u.platform_ids.items()}
  77→
  78→    # -- DirectoryIndex protocol (connectors/_http.py) ------------------------------------------
  79→    def get(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[DirectoryUser]:
  80→        return self._users.get(user_id)
  81→
  82→    def by_platform_id(self, platform: str, native_id: str) -> Optional[DirectoryUser]:
  83→        uid = self._by_native.get((platform, native_id))
  84→        return self._users.get(uid) if uid else None
  85→
  86→    def all(self) -> list[DirectoryUser]:
  87→        return list(self._users.values())
  88→
  89→    # -- mutation (webhook user.changed / admin) ------------------------------------------------
  90→    def set_active(self, user_id: str, active: bool) -> None:
  91→        with self._lock:
  92→            u = self._users.get(user_id)
  93→            if u is None or u.active == active:
  94→                return
  95→            self._users[user_id] = u.model_copy(update={"active": active})
  96→            self.epoch += 1
  97→

1→"""Slack connector (A3) — supported subset per plan §4.5.
   2→
   3→Documents: one ``SourceDoc`` per THREAD, ``doc_id = "slack:<channel>:<thread_ts>"``.
   4→
   5→Permission semantics compiled into ``AclExpr``:
   6→* public channel  → ``any(users(members), all(kind(member), everyone))`` — every full member of the
   7→  workspace, plus guests / Connect users only if they are in the channel;
   8→* private channel and Slack Connect (``is_ext_shared``) channel → ``users(members)``;
   9→* archived channel → unchanged (still readable by whoever could read it);
  10→* DMs / group DMs / anything not returned by ``conversations.list`` → ``nobody`` (unsupported).
  11→  ``is_im`` / ``is_mpim`` are checked FIRST, before private / shared (a private-flagged group DM is
  12→  still a DM); a channel object missing any of ``is_im``, ``is_mpim``, ``is_private``,
  13→  ``is_ext_shared`` (or carrying a non-boolean) is UNCLASSIFIED → ``nobody`` / deny, never "public"
  14→  (Codex sec3a #2, #3).
  15→
  16→Gate 2 asks Slack itself (``users.info`` + ``conversations.list`` + ``conversations.members`` +
  17→``conversations.replies``) on every call — one attempt each, 2 s timeout, any failure denies. The
  18→returned user / channel ids must be the ones asked for, and ``deleted``, ``is_restricted``,
  19→``is_ultra_restricted`` and ``is_stranger`` must all be present booleans, else deny.
  20→
  21→Thread version (``SourceDoc.version``): ``"<latest ts>|<message count>|<digest>"`` where the digest
  22→covers every message's ts, edit ts, author and text — deleting or editing ANY message (not only the
  23→newest) changes it, so Gate 2 reports drift (Codex sec3a #6). The crawler compares the parent's
  24→``reply_count`` with the stored count, so a deleted reply is re-fetched even when the latest-reply
  25→ts does not move; an edit to an older reply that Slack does not surface on the parent is caught by
  26→Gate 2's drift check on the next answer (and the full reconciliation of the next re-fetch).
  27→"""
  28→from __future__ import annotations
  29→
  30→import hashlib
  31→import json
  32→import re
  33→from typing import Any, Mapping, Optional, Sequence
  34→
  35→import httpx
  36→
  37→from .. import acl as A

  52→

 113→                 workspace_host: str = "companya.slack.com", sleep=None, now=None):

 132→    def _ingest(self, method: str, params: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:

 149→    def _paged(self, method: str, params: dict[str, Any], key: str, *, gate2: bool = False,
 150→               stop=None) -> list[Any]:
 151→        out: list[Any] = []
 152→        cursor = ""
 153→        guard = PageGuard(f"slack {method}", gate2=gate2)
 154→        while True:
 155→            guard.next_page(cursor)                 # cap / cursor cycle ⇒ raise, never a partial
 156→            p = dict(params, **({"cursor": cursor} if cursor else {}))
 157→            data = self._gate2(method, p) if gate2 else self._ingest(method, p)
 158→            if not data.get("ok", False):

 161→                    raise SourceFailure("gone" if err in _GONE else "source_error", detail=err)

 165→            page = data.get(key)
 166→            if page is None:
 167→                page = []
 168→            if not isinstance(page, list):
 169→                if gate2:
 170→                    raise SourceFailure("source_bad_payload", detail=f"{method}.{key}")

 354→                       ("deleted", "is_restricted", "is_ultra_restricted", "is_stranger")):
 355→                return verdict("forbidden", "source_bad_payload")    # missing flags never widen
 356→            if su["deleted"]:

 364→            ch = self._channel(channel, gate2=True)
 365→            if ch is None:

 367→            kind = _channel_kind(ch)
 368→            if kind == "dm":

 415→    def list_changes(self, cursor: Optional[str]) -> ChangeBatch:
 416→        """Re-lists every channel and thread parent each time (so deletions are seen) and fetches
 417→        replies only for threads whose latest-reply ts moved. Cursor JSON::
 418→
 419→            {"v":1, "channels": {"<C>": {"kind": "public|private|connect", "archived": bool,
 420→                                         "members": [native ids], "latest": "<max ts>",
 421→                                         "threads": {"<thread ts>": "<version>"}}}}
 422→        """
 423→        prev = self._load_cursor(cursor)
 424→        prev_ch: dict[str, Any] = (prev or {}).get("channels", {})
 425→        docs: list[SourceDoc] = []
 426→        deleted: list[str] = []
 427→        acl_changed: list[str] = []
 428→        new_ch: dict[str, Any] = {}
 429→
 430→        for ch in self._channels():
 431→            cid = ch["id"]
 432→            kind = _channel_kind(ch)
 433→            if kind in UNSUPPORTED_KINDS:                  # DM / unclassified: never indexed
 434→                continue
 435→            members = self._members(cid)
 436→            old = prev_ch.get(cid) or {}
 437→            old_threads: dict[str, str] = old.get("threads", {}) if old else {}
 438→            threads: dict[str, str] = {}
 439→            try:
 440→                parents = self._paged("conversations.history", {"channel": cid, "limit": 200}, "messages")
 441→            except _Gone:
 442→                parents = []
 443→            for p in parents:
 444→                if not isinstance(p, dict) or not p.get("ts"):
 445→                    continue
 446→                if p.get("thread_ts") and p.get("thread_ts") != p.get("ts"):
 447→                    continue                                # a broadcast reply, not a parent
 448→                ts = str(p["ts"])
 449→                hint = str(p.get("latest_reply") or ts)
 450→                if isinstance(p.get("edited"), dict) and p["edited"].get("ts"):
 451→                    hint = max(hint, str(p["edited"]["ts"]), key=_ts_key)
 452→                old_v = old_threads.get(ts)
 453→                rc = p.get("reply_count")
 454→                if rc is None and not p.get("latest_reply") and not p.get("thread_ts"):
 455→                    rc = 0                                # a plain message: Slack omits the count
 456→                same_count = (isinstance(rc, int) and not isinstance(rc, bool)
 457→                              and version_count(old_v) == rc + 1)
 458→                if (old_v is not None and same_count
 459→                        and _ts_key(version_ts(old_v)) >= _ts_key(hint)):
 460→                    threads[ts] = old_v                   # nothing newer, nothing deleted
 461→                    continue
 462→                msgs = self._replies(cid, ts)
 463→                if not msgs:
 464→                    continue
 465→                doc = self._build_doc(ch, ts, msgs)
 466→                if doc.version != old_v:                  # re-fetched but unchanged: not re-emitted
 467→                    docs.append(doc)
 468→                threads[ts] = doc.version
 469→            for ts in old_threads:
 470→                if ts not in threads:
 471→                    deleted.append(thread_doc_id(cid, ts))
 472→            if old and (old.get("members") != members or old.get("kind") != kind
 473→                        or bool(old.get("archived")) != bool(ch.get("is_archived"))):
 474→                # every surviving doc of the channel (content-changed ones too: their ACL moved as well)
 475→                acl_changed.extend(thread_doc_id(cid, ts) for ts in threads if ts in old_threads)
 476→            new_ch[cid] = {"kind": kind, "archived": bool(ch.get("is_archived")), "members": members,
 477→                           "latest": (max((version_ts(v) for v in threads.values()), key=_ts_key)
 478→                                      if threads else ""),
 479→                           "threads": threads}
 480→        for cid, old in prev_ch.items():
 481→            if cid not in new_ch:
 482→                deleted.extend(thread_doc_id(cid, ts) for ts in (old.get("threads") or {}))
 483→        new_cursor = json.dumps({"v": CURSOR_VERSION, "channels": new_ch}, sort_keys=True,
 484→                                separators=(",", ":"))
 485→        return ChangeBatch(docs=tuple(docs), deleted=tuple(deleted), acl_changed=tuple(acl_changed),
 486→                           cursor=new_cursor)

1→"""Shared plumbing for the IB connectors (A3): HTTP calls, webhook verification, link extraction.
   2→
   3→Two HTTP disciplines, deliberately different:
   4→
   5→* **Ingest** (``request_ingest``): retries 429 honouring ``Retry-After`` and retries 5xx/transport
   6→  errors with a short backoff. The crawler can afford to wait.
   7→* **Gate 2** (``request_gate2``): exactly ONE attempt with a hard timeout. Any failure surfaces as
   8→  ``SourceFailure`` so the caller can deny with a reason code. Gate 2 never waits out a rate limit.
   9→
  10→Webhooks: ``X-IB-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, f"{ts}.{delivery}.{body}")>`` — the
  11→delivery id is INSIDE the MAC (Codex sec3 #8/#11: otherwise one captured delivery could be replayed
  12→under fresh ids) — ``X-IB-Timestamp`` within ±300 s, ``X-IB-Delivery`` never seen before. The
  13→replay set is in-process: a second worker or a restart can accept the same delivery once more inside
  14→the window (documented in SECURITY.md; events only invalidate, so a replay costs work, not access).
  15→
  16→Pagination: every paged loop goes through ``PageGuard`` — a page cap or a repeated cursor raises
  17→(``ConnectorError`` on ingest, ``SourceFailure("source_incomplete")`` at Gate 2): a partial listing is
  18→never returned as if it were complete (Codex sec3a #12, sec3b #6).
  19→"""

  95→class PageGuard:
  96→    """Bounds a cursor loop: ``next_page(cursor)`` before each request after the first. Raises when
  97→    the cap is hit with pages remaining or a cursor repeats (a cycle) — never a silent partial."""
  98→
  99→    def __init__(self, what: str, *, gate2: bool = False, max_pages: Optional[int] = None):
 100→        self.what = what
 101→        self.gate2 = gate2
 102→        self.max_pages = max_pages if max_pages is not None else MAX_PAGES
 103→        self.pages = 0
 104→        self._seen: set[str] = set()

 106→    def _fail(self, why: str) -> Exception:
 107→        if self.gate2:
 108→            return SourceFailure("source_incomplete", detail=f"{self.what}: {why}")
 109→        return ConnectorError(f"{self.what}: {why} — listing incomplete")

 111→    def next_page(self, cursor: Any) -> None:
 112→        """Account for one more request (with ``cursor``; '' for the first)."""
 113→        self.pages += 1
 114→        if self.pages > self.max_pages:
 115→            raise self._fail(f"more than {self.max_pages} pages")
 116→        key = str(cursor or "")
 117→        if key:
 118→            if key in self._seen:
 119→                raise self._fail("pagination cursor repeated")
 120→            self._seen.add(key)

 143→def request_ingest(client: httpx.Client, method: str, url: str, *, params: Any = None,
 144→                   json_body: Any = None, attempts: int = 5, max_wait_s: float = 30.0,
 145→                   sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
 146→                   ok_statuses: tuple[int, ...] = ()) -> httpx.Response:
 147→    """Ingest call with retries. Returns the response for 2xx (or a status in ``ok_statuses``,
 148→    e.g. 404 the caller wants to interpret); raises ``ConnectorError`` once retries are spent."""
 149→    last = "no attempt"
 150→    for attempt in range(attempts):
 151→        try:
 152→            resp = client.request(method, url, params=params, json=json_body)
 153→        except httpx.HTTPError as exc:                              # transport / timeout
 154→            last = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
 155→            if attempt + 1 < attempts:
 156→                sleep(min(max_wait_s, 0.5 * (2 ** attempt)))
 157→            continue
 158→        if resp.status_code == 429:
 159→            last = "429 rate limited"
 160→            if attempt + 1 < attempts:
 161→                sleep(min(max_wait_s, _retry_after_s(resp, 1.0)))
 162→            continue
 163→        if resp.status_code >= 500:
 164→            last = f"{resp.status_code} server error"
 165→            if attempt + 1 < attempts:
 166→                sleep(min(max_wait_s, 0.5 * (2 ** attempt)))
 167→            continue
 168→        if resp.is_success or resp.status_code in ok_statuses:
 169→            return resp
 170→        raise ConnectorError(f"{method} {url} -> {resp.status_code}")
 171→    raise ConnectorError(f"{method} {url} failed after {attempts} attempts: {last}")

 178→    status listed in ``ok_statuses``, which the caller interprets itself)."""

 182→        raise SourceFailure("source_timeout", detail=str(exc)) from exc
 183→    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:

 185→    if resp.status_code == 429:

 187→    if resp.is_success or resp.status_code in ok_statuses:

 204→def sign_webhook(secret: str, timestamp: Union[int, str], delivery_id: str, body: bytes) -> str:
 205→    """``sha256=<hex>`` over ``f"{timestamp}.{delivery_id}.{body}"``, exactly as the mock signs it
 206→    (also used by tests). The delivery id is authenticated, so it cannot be swapped on a replay."""
 207→    msg = str(timestamp).encode() + b"." + str(delivery_id).encode() + b"." + body
 208→    return "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), msg, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

 219→class WebhookVerifier:
 220→    """Signature (over timestamp + delivery id + body) + ±300 s window + replayed-delivery set.
 221→    Thread-safe; replay memory is bounded to ids whose timestamps are still inside the window
 222→    (older ones fail the window check anyway). The set is PER PROCESS: multi-worker / restart replay
 223→    inside the window is a documented limitation (SECURITY.md, track 3 disposition)."""
 224→
 225→    def __init__(self, secret: str, *, window_s: int = WEBHOOK_WINDOW_S,
 226→                 now: Callable[[], float] = time.time):
 227→        if not secret:
 228→            raise ValueError("webhook secret is required")
 229→        self._secret = secret
 230→        self._window = window_s
 231→        self._now = now
 232→        self._seen: dict[str, float] = {}
 233→        self._lock = threading.Lock()
 234→
 235→    def verify(self, headers: Mapping[str, str], body: bytes) -> tuple[str, int]:
 236→        delivery = _header(headers, "X-IB-Delivery").strip()
 237→        ts_raw = _header(headers, "X-IB-Timestamp").strip()
 238→        sig = _header(headers, "X-IB-Signature").strip()
 239→        if not delivery or not ts_raw or not sig:
 240→            raise WebhookRejected("missing signature headers")
 241→        try:
 242→            ts = int(ts_raw)
 243→        except ValueError as exc:
 244→            raise WebhookRejected("bad timestamp") from exc
 245→        expected = sign_webhook(self._secret, ts_raw, delivery, body)
 246→        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected.encode(), sig.encode()):
 247→            raise WebhookRejected("bad signature")
 248→        now = self._now()
 249→        if abs(now - ts) > self._window:
 250→            raise WebhookRejected("stale timestamp")
 251→        with self._lock:
 252→            for d, seen_ts in list(self._seen.items()):
 253→                if now - seen_ts > 2 * self._window:
 254→                    del self._seen[d]
 255→            if delivery in self._seen:
 256→                raise WebhookRejected("replayed delivery")
 257→            self._seen[delivery] = float(ts)
 258→        return delivery, ts

 298→def extract_links(text: str, *, slack_host: str = "companya.slack.com",
 299→                  confluence_host: str = "companya.atlassian.net",
 300→                  drive_host: str = "docs.google.com") -> tuple[str, ...]:
 301→    """Supported identifiers in ``text``, de-duplicated in first-seen order:
 302→
 303→    * Jira keys ``ABC-123``                              → ``jira:ABC-123``
 304→    * ``https://<confluence_host>/wiki/.../pages/<id>``   → ``confluence:<id>``
 305→    * ``https://<slack_host>/archives/<C..>/p<16 digits>`` → ``slack:<channel>:<thread ts>``
 306→      (``?thread_ts=`` wins, so a permalink to a reply resolves to its thread)
 307→    * ``https://<drive_host>/<kind>/d/<id>``             → ``drive:<id>``
 308→
 309→    Any other URL — other hosts, look-alike hosts, other path shapes — is ignored.
 310→    """
 311→    out: list[str] = []
 312→
 313→    def add(x: str) -> None:
 314→        if x not in out:
 315→            out.append(x)
 316→
 317→    for m in _URL.finditer(text or ""):
 318→        url = m.group(0).rstrip(".,;:!?")
 319→        try:
 320→            u = urlparse(url)
 321→        except ValueError:
 322→            continue
 323→        host = (u.hostname or "").lower()
 324→        parts = [p for p in u.path.split("/") if p]
 325→        if host == confluence_host and parts[:1] == ["wiki"]:
 326→            if "pages" in parts:
 327→                i = parts.index("pages")
 328→                if i + 1 < len(parts) and _ID.match(parts[i + 1]):
 329→                    add(f"confluence:{parts[i + 1]}")
 330→        elif host == slack_host and len(parts) >= 3 and parts[0] == "archives":
 331→            chan, msg = parts[1], parts[2]
 332→            mm = _SLACK_TS.match(msg)
 333→            if _ID.match(chan) and mm:
 334→                ts = f"{mm.group(1)}.{mm.group(2)}"
 335→                tts = parse_qs(u.query).get("thread_ts", [""])[0]
 336→                if re.fullmatch(r"\d{10}\.\d{6}", tts or ""):
 337→                    ts = tts
 338→                add(f"slack:{chan}:{ts}")
 339→        elif host == drive_host and len(parts) >= 3 and parts[1] == "d" and _ID.match(parts[2]):
 340→            add(f"drive:{parts[2]}")
 341→    for m in _JIRA_KEY.finditer(text or ""):
 342→        add(f"jira:{m.group(1)}")
 343→    return tuple(out)
